title: Boycotting Carrefour: A-to-Z of supporting Israel and Hyperstar's proxy presence in the Iranian market
summary: An introduction to Carrefour, documentation of its support for Israel, and Hyperstar's proxy presence in the Iranian market, citing official sources.

data.text: Hyperstar: Carrefour's shadow in Iran's sky

data.caption: Hyperstar's Iran Mall branch in Tehran

data.text: We all know Hyperstar — the chain store that has been in Iran since 2009 (1388 in the Iranian calendar) and is known for its good discounts, brand variety and complete range. In recent years Hyperstar has also launched a strategic partnership with Snapp under the Snapp Market brand in the online-sales space, aiming to grow its Iranian market share. The MyliMarket brand, a Hyperstar subsidiary, has for some time also been active in the Iranian market to compete with smaller stores. It might be a big claim if someone said by shopping at Hyperstar you're helping the Israeli economy! — right in the heart of Israel's biggest enemy, Iran. An enemy that has repeatedly come close to direct military confrontation with Israel. In this note we examine this surprising claim together. Stay with us.
Chapter one: Carrefour is proud!

"Carrefour is proud to have opened 50 stores in Israel today and to continue its international growth strategy [in Israel]. Israel is now the fifty-second country in which Carrefour operates across the world, thanks in particular to our franchise partners. We are confident that Carrefour will help Israeli customers who have been affected by the cost-of-living crisis."
data.caption: Alexandre Bompard, Chairman and CEO of the Carrefour Group / 9 May 2023 (Source: Carrefour official website)
Bompard's quote on Carrefour's official website

data.text: The name Carrefour may sound familiar. The French chain-store giant is the oldest retail chain in the world and the seventh most valuable brand in the retail industry. Carrefour today has more than 13,900 outlets across the world (Source: Carrefour Group website), and it has been accused of supporting the Israeli regime for years, a fixture on lists of brands supporting this regime. But how can a chain of stores help the Israeli economy?

The quote at the top of this article is from Alexandre Bompard, Chairman of Carrefour. In these words he refers to Carrefour's presence in Israel with the help of its partners. He also says that Carrefour's presence in the occupied territories can help Israelis affected by the cost-of-living crisis.

According to information published by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), in 2022 Israel had the highest cost of living among the 38 OECD countries — even surpassing Switzerland! This issue is known as the cost-of-living crisis in Israel.
data.caption: Source: Israeli network i24

data.text: Israel's economy, due to its dependence on imports in sectors such as food and agriculture, is highly uncompetitive and monopolistic. This monopoly has continuously raised the cost-of-living index in recent years. The issue, known in Israel as the cost-of-living crisis, has made many dual-passport citizens hesitant to choose Israel as a place to live. Food prices in Israel have risen 50% over the past two decades and are 25% to 80% above the OECD average, with dairy products, soft drinks and grain-based products especially expensive. In the food-retail sector, three local supermarket chains hold more than half the Israeli market. This monopoly limits competition and pushes prices up. (Source)
Imagine you live in Israel and face all sorts of insecurity every day — while paying Swiss cost-of-living prices!
Carrefour steps in

This is where Carrefour steps onto the field. Carrefour, with its broad international supply chain, can lower the cost of supplying goods and come to the aid of Israeli citizens — exactly what Carrefour's CEO referred to. This is so important to the Zionists in propaganda terms that, occasionally, officials at the level of prime minister or economy minister attend the opening of Carrefour branches! In its advertising Carrefour claims that an equivalent shopping basket can be delivered to consumers up to 60% cheaper than its local competitors. (The Times of Israel)

data.caption: Israeli Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Industry at the Beit Shemesh branch of Carrefour Israel at its official opening / 8 May 2023

data.text: In the photos above, Netanyahu is pointing to the shopping-basket bill that Carrefour claims came in 60% cheaper. The Carrefour logo at the top of the list on the right, and the number 59.3% off at the top of the banner, stand out. (Source: official Israeli-government website)
"We are convinced that Carrefour Israel will offer a real solution for Israeli consumers and significantly improve their purchasing power."
data.caption: Patrick Lasfargues / Head of Carrefour's International Division (Source: The Times of Israel)

data.text: The presence of a reputable, global, well-known brand like Carrefour can be seen as a symbol of the Israeli regime's leaders' efforts to counter the cost-of-living crisis — perhaps similar to the Abraham Accords as a symbol of breaking Israel's political isolation.

But this is not Carrefour's only charge. Carrefour has various cooperation models for its international presence. One of these is using local partners and so-called franchising. Which brings us to Carrefour's second case-file.
Carrefour partners up

In Carrefour's partnership model, it usually enters a 50-50 joint venture with a local competitor, and all of that competitor's branches are switched over to Carrefour signage and supply chain. But who is Carrefour's partner in Israel?
On 8 March 2022, the Carrefour Group unveiled a new franchise agreement in Israel with Electra / Electra Consumer Products and its subsidiary Yenot Bitan.

Both companies are serious participants in illegal settlement-building and partners to the occupation by Israeli settlers. Their names are listed by the United Nations as commercial partners of illegal settlement-building. (Source: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights)

data.caption: The name of one of Electra's subsidiaries on the UN list of participants in illegal settlement-building

data.text: Electra is a large Israeli holding with serious involvement in Israeli settlement and government projects, and it also supplies the needs of settlers. The decision to partner with Electra has led to Carrefour being accused of complicity in the occupiers' settler activities.
The reason Carrefour's name appears on every list of Zionist-goods boycotts — including BDS — is precisely this partnership with Electra. (BDS)
OK, so let's say by now we have understood what role Carrefour plays in Israel's survival. So what does any of this have to do with Hyperstar and us Iranians? Are we Carrefour customers too?
Chapter two: Hyperstar, the Islamic Carrefour!
Majid Al Futtaim and Carrefour in Iran

As mentioned earlier, one of Carrefour's expansion models is partnership and joint investment with local partners. Carrefour's expansion in our region follows the same pattern. The Emirati holding Majid Al Futtaim (MAF) is Carrefour's strategic partner in the Middle East, and many of the region's branches — from North Africa to West Asia — have been opened through partnership with this very holding.

Majid Al Futtaim operates in shopping centres, hypermarkets and hotels. The company built a key partnership with Carrefour from the start of its founding. In 2013, MAF paid 2.5 billion dirhams ($530 million) to acquire a 25% stake in the French giant.

In 2009 (1388 in the Iranian calendar), MAF and Carrefour opened the first Carrefour branch in Iran — in Tehran, under the name Hyperstar. That branch was launched with a 49-51 partnership in eastern Tehran, with an unnamed Iranian partner. Of the 49% foreign side, 25% belongs to MAF and 24% to Carrefour. (Daily News Egypt)
In May 2007, the CEO of MAF's shopping-centres division gave an interesting interview to Arabian Business about their presence in Iran:

"The French hypermarket group Carrefour has committed to opening its first hypermarket in Iran, and the retail arm of Majid Al Futtaim (MAF) — which runs Carrefour stores in the Middle East — has also committed to the project."
data.caption: Source: Arabian Business

data.text: Green instead of blue!

But why has Carrefour used the Hyperstar brand instead of its own primary brand in Iran? This brand was previously used in Pakistan's Carrefour branch too, until 2019 when Hyperstar Pakistan rebranded to Carrefour Pakistan. (Pakistani news outlet The Express Tribune)

The reason for this naming choice is not entirely clear, but Carrefour officials have hinted at it in interviews. They have said the reason for the rebrand was fear of Muslim-country sensitivities towards Western businesses. (Daily News Egypt)

Carrefour, by way of Hyperstar's proxy presence, is active in the Iranian market and offers services such as retail. These are services that on their surface aren't particularly complex or technological, and large well-known domestic competitors already provide similar services.
